svg.title: Denford CNC 2600 Pro individual-conductor retrofit diagram
svg.desc: Exact controller, interface, driver, supply and machine terminal labels are joined by separate conductors. Dotted routes are proposed unverified guesses. OPEN breaks identify the missing connection. Numbering is logical, not a mating-face view.

P1 1/3 are positive opto inputs, commonly tied to +5 V; P1 2/4 are sink inputs. P2 terminal functions are GND,+V,A+,A\u2212,B+,B\u2212. Core uses logic signals only; +37 V stays at driver P2. U1 drives X and Y (four channels): at the MSD556 specified 7\u201316 mA input range, worst-case sum is 64 mA, below a conservative 100 mA package-ground design budget; still verify TI guaranteed output-low limits. This proposal supplies PUL+/DIR+ from the new regulated 5V logic distribution, with its return wired to buffer/Core logic GND, so no unidentified old-controller supply contact is required. Driver motor power remains separate. U2 reserves its first two channels for Z; X/Y use four output channels on U1. Their combined worst-case MSD556 input sink current is 64 mA on U1; Z is at most 32 mA on U2 using 16 mA per input, subject to TI recommended operating conditions. P1 1/3 are positive opto inputs, commonly tied to +5 V; P1 2/4 are sink inputs. P2 terminal functions are GND,+V,A+,A\u2212,B+,B\u2212. Core uses logic signals only; +37 V stays at driver P2. text.tspan: Denford CNC 2600 Pro · individual conductor plan

svg.text: Dotted = GUESS / proposed conversion, verify before energizing · Green = retained source path · Broken = OPEN
Each circle is one named physical pin, terminal or identified lead. Connector orientation and fitted revision must match.
Crossing lines are not junctions. Connections exist only at the named terminal circles and explicitly shared nets.

text.tspan: Controller logic supply · separate from motor power

svg.text: Verify exact board supply path and rail ratings; motor current uses separate wiring and fuses.

text.tspan: MSD556 X STEP/DIR and motor power · conditional axis mapping

svg.text: OPEN
The Baldor source does not map each physical MSD556 to X/Y/Z. P1 1/3 are positive opto inputs, commonly tied to +5 V; P1 2/4
are sink inputs. P2 terminal functions are GND,+V,A+,A−,B+,B−. Core uses logic signals only; +37 V stays at driver P2. U1
drives X and Y (four channels): at the MSD556 specified 7–16 mA input range, worst-case sum is 64 mA, below a conservative
100 mA package-ground design budget; still verify TI guaranteed output-low limits. This proposal supplies PUL+/DIR+ from the
new regulated 5V logic distribution, with its return wired to buffer/Core logic GND, so no unidentified old-controller supply
contact is required. Driver motor power remains separate. Opto input current and timing still require measurement.

text.tspan: MSD556 X driver · supply and motor winding chain

svg.text: Never connect legacy +37 V to Core or Prime logic/power. The mapped contact functions are motor-stage outputs; axis and
individual cable identities remain unverified.

text.tspan: MSD556 Y STEP/DIR and motor power · conditional axis mapping

svg.text: OPEN
The Baldor source does not map each physical MSD556 to X/Y/Z. P1 1/3 are positive opto inputs, commonly tied to +5 V; P1 2/4
are sink inputs. P2 terminal functions are GND,+V,A+,A−,B+,B−. Core uses logic signals only; +37 V stays at driver P2. U1 is
shared with X only (four active outputs total; 64 mA worst case at 16 mA/input). This proposal supplies PUL+/DIR+ from the
new regulated 5V logic distribution, with its return wired to buffer/Core logic GND, so no unidentified old-controller supply
contact is required. Driver motor power remains separate. Opto input current and timing still require measurement.

text.tspan: MSD556 Y driver · supply and motor winding chain

svg.text: Never connect legacy +37 V to Core or Prime logic/power. The mapped contact functions are motor-stage outputs; axis and
individual cable identities remain unverified.

text.tspan: MSD556 Z STEP/DIR and motor power · conditional axis mapping

svg.text: OPEN
Z driver-to-axis mapping is a dotted proposal pending cable tracing. U2 reserves its first two channels for Z; X/Y use four
output channels on U1. Their combined worst-case MSD556 input sink current is 64 mA on U1; Z is at most 32 mA on U2 using 16
mA per input, subject to TI recommended operating conditions. P1 1/3 are positive opto inputs, commonly tied to +5 V; P1 2/4
are sink inputs. P2 terminal functions are GND,+V,A+,A−,B+,B−. Core uses logic signals only; +37 V stays at driver P2. This
proposal supplies PUL+/DIR+ from the new regulated 5V logic distribution, with its return wired to buffer/Core logic GND, so
no unidentified old-controller supply contact is required. Driver motor power remains separate. Opto input current and timing
still require measurement.

text.tspan: MSD556 Z driver · supply and motor winding chain

svg.text: Never connect legacy +37 V to Core or Prime logic/power. The mapped contact functions are motor-stage outputs; axis and
individual cable identities remain unverified.

text.tspan: Baldor VS1ST · Core PWM to spindle speed analog input
Rf 20kΩ terminal A · U3 pin6 side
Rf 20kΩ terminal B · U3 pin2 side
Rg 10kΩ terminal A · U3 pin2 side

svg.text: Baldor VS1ST MN767 Table 1-1 p.1-4: terminal 6 = analog input 1; 7 and 9 = common (internally connected); terminal 5 is +10 V
ref but is not an output command source. Converter is a hand-built proposal using TI OPA197 SOIC-8 exact pins, R1 10kΩ/C1
10µF, Rf20k/Rg10k; it needs schematic review and bench test. OPA197 SOIC-8 NC pins 1, 5 and 8 are not connected. Fit local
100 nF bypass between U3 pins7 and4, plus nearby bulk capacitance chosen for supply impedance. R1/C1 time constant is 0.1 s:
verify ripple and speed response at chosen PWM frequency. Sequence supplies so GPIO does not drive an unpowered stage; prove
zero-command/startup output and loss-of-command shutdown.

text.tspan: Baldor VS1ST · separate run contact, safety, power and spindle boundary

svg.text: Cabinet Wiring maps original J5 control-board pins11/12 to VS1ST 7/6 and says terminal1 +24 V is switched to terminal2 for
drive enable. This is a reported original path, not proof of current cabinet wiring. Preserve physical E-stop, door/guard,
contactor and relay chain. The spindle motor is on VS1ST U/T1,V/T2,W/T3 and PE, never on Smoothie; exact installed motor/line
variant and terminal mapping require the nameplate/manual. See the separate fully named ULN2003AN/AQY212GS process-run
proposal; no generic unspecified relay is needed.

text.tspan: Denford limit, door and E-stop chain · do not repurpose from screenshot
door/pump relay path and contact unknown
Z brake output path; revision/axis mapping

svg.text: OPEN
OPEN
OPEN
The currently functional flag and retrofit plans do not prove which controller/relay revision is installed. The MRP-0850B
drawing is Rev B while the machine may be Rev A; do not join or infer safety contacts from the wrong revision.

text.tspan: Isolated run LED drive · power, bias and every IC pin

svg.text: New engineering proposal: Core GPIO → ULN2003AN → AQY212GS LED, isolated contact pins3/4 to configured machine run circuit.
This slow process interface does not implement E-stop, STO or PWM. Verify startup inactive, receiver mode/current, isolation
layout and loaded off-state leakage before use. Nominal 390 Ω limits LED to approximately 5.5–9 mA using conservative 4.75 V
supply, 1.5 V LED and 1.1 V sink drop assumptions; recheck tolerance/temperature and actual sink voltage. AQY212GS
recommended LED5–30mA, contact≤48V/1A at25°C, derate by temperature; measured receiver current must fit. Contact is
bidirectional and galvanically isolated from the LED side: no logic ground crosses that barrier.

text.tspan: Isolated run contact · machine side only

svg.text: These contact pins belong to the same U6 used in the preceding LED-drive panel. The optically isolated contact side has no
conductor to Core or ULN logic GND. Retain independent hardware stop/safety. Verify receiver mode and off-state leakage; this
is a new unverified process-run proposal.

text.tspan: Buffer bypass and every unused CMOS input

svg.text: Same ICs as the preceding axis panels. Local 100nF bypass beside each VCC/GND pair; unused CMOS inputs tied to logic GND and
open-drain outputs left unconnected. Never feed opto +5V into 3V3 VCC. Measured package-current and GPIO/rail budgets must
fit recommended operating conditions.

text.tspan: Denford · retained guard, limit and brake boundaries · source revision check
J13.5 · ground to release Z brake

svg.text: OPEN
OPEN
OPEN
These are individual source reference contacts, not a claim that the old controller is still fitted. Maintain the physical
E-stop/guard/contactor chain. Z brake releases when energized; no unqualified Core output may command brake or door unlock.
Trace and document the current relay board, contact ratings and fail-safe behavior first. The separate VS1 run proposal is a
process command and does not bypass this retained machine safety/enable chain.
Read the exact per-wire schedule, full contact inventory, parts, configuration and source checks in the accompanying profile.
